<figure id="A1.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2502.19645v1/fig/fold_shorts--eval_initial_positions.png" id="A1.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/143;" width="476" height="143" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Fig. 9: </span><span id="A1.F9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Initial states for “fold shorts” task evaluations.</span> We use the smallest variance in initial positions for this task due to the small number of training demonstrations (20) compared to other tasks. During the first eight rollouts, the shorts’ position is incrementally adjusted by up to 3 cm along the vertical axis of the tabletop surface. In the final two rollouts, the shorts are rotated 10 degrees clockwise to align the bottom edge to be parallel to the tabletop’s horizontal axis.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A1.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2502.19645v1/fig/fold_shirt--eval_initial_positions.png" id="A1.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/143;" width="476" height="143" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Fig. 10: </span><span id="A1.F10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Initial states for “fold shirt” task evaluations.</span> The bottom edge of the shirt varies by 15 cm along the tabletop’s vertical axis across different trials.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A1.F11" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2502.19645v1/fig/scoop_x_into_bowl--eval_initial_positions.png" id="A1.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:381/381;" width="381" height="381" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Fig. 11: </span><span id="A1.F11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Initial states for “scoop X into bowl” task evaluations.</span> The green bowl’s position varies by up to 10 cm across both vertical and horizontal table axes. Simultaneously, the metal spoon’s position varies by 3 cm along the horizontal axis. Each row in this grid displays a set of three identical initial states since we rotate among three target food ingredients (“raisins”, “almonds and green M&amp;Ms”, and “pretzels”) with the same initial states, before moving on to the next set of initial states.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A1.F12" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2502.19645v1/fig/put_x_into_pot--eval_initial_positions.png" id="A1.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:381/381;" width="381" height="381" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Fig. 12: </span><span id="A1.F12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Initial states for “put X into pot” task evaluations (in-distribution version).</span> Food object positions vary by 15 cm vertically and 40 cm horizontally across trials, while the pot remains stationary. Each grid row presents three identical initial states, as we cycle through the three target objects (“green pepper”, “red pepper”, and “yellow corn”) using the same initial configurations before we move on to the next set of initial configurations. (Refer to Figure <a href="#A1.F13" title="Fig. 13 ‣ A-G Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> for the out-of-distribution version of this task.)</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A1.F13" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2502.19645v1/fig/put_x_into_pot--ood--eval_initial_positions.png" id="A1.F13.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:381/381;" width="381" height="381" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Fig. 13: </span><span id="A1.F13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Initial states for “put X into pot” task evaluations (out-of-distribution version).</span> Unlike the in-distribution version of this task (Figure <a href="#A1.F12" title="Fig. 12 ‣ A-G Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>), this version introduces unseen green and orange bowls as distractor objects to assess robustness to novel visual inputs. Food object positions vary by 15 cm vertically and 30 cm horizontally across trials, with the pot remaining stationary. Each grid row presents three identical initial states, as we cycle through the three target objects (“green pepper”, “red pepper”, and “yellow corn”) using the same initial configurations before we move on to the next set of initial configurations.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A1.T10" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">TABLE X: </span><span id="A1.T10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Detailed results for the “fold shorts” ALOHA task.</span> Success is assessed using a staged scoring system, with 20 points allocated to each of five task stages. Points are awarded cumulatively, requiring successful completion of prior stages to receive a nonzero score in subsequent stages. The reported values represent the average performance across all experimental trials.</figcaption>

<figure id="A1.T11" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">TABLE XI: </span><span id="A1.T11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Detailed results for the “fold shirt” ALOHA task.</span> Success is assessed using a staged scoring system, with 10 points allocated to each of ten task stages. Points are awarded cumulatively, requiring successful completion of prior stages to receive a nonzero score in subsequent stages. A penalty of -10 points is applied if a large portion of the shirt sticks out after the final fold, as this is a common error for one method and is visually apparent. The reported values represent the average performance across all experimental trials.</figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">TABLE XII: </span><span id="A1.T12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Detailed results for the “scoop X into bowl” ALOHA task.</span> Success is assessed using a staged scoring system. <figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">TABLE XIV: </span><span id="A1.T14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Ablation experiment: fine-tuning OpenVLA from scratch with the OFT recipe.</span> Policy inputs here include a third-person camera image, a wrist camera image, robot proprioceptive state, and a language instruction. The from-scratch policies generally perform worse than the full OpenVLA-OFT policies, confirming that OpenVLA’s pretrained representation is beneficial for downstream policy performance even when the fine-tuning recipe differs substantially from the pretraining recipe.</figcaption>

      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
